config.title: Is one-sided key-norm the strictly-better attention norm? k-norm-only vs QK-norm across the full head split
config.hypothesis: 2026-08-23 found that at nh=1, norming ONE side beats norming none and both: k-norm-only -0.041 bpc vs baseline (3/3 seeds, 4-8x lower variance), q-norm-only -0.019, while full QK-norm pays a +0.073 q x k interaction term. Nobody checked multi-head. Tonight the four norm arms (baseline / qknorm / qnorm_only / knorm_only) run across the full iso-parameter head-split family n_head x head_dim = 128 (hd 4/16/32/64 fresh, hd 128 imported from the bit-exact 08-23 run after live verification), 3 seeds, byte-identical paired inits. Predictions from the thread's mechanism story: (1) if the hd=4 cliff is q-side per-token magnitude destruction (08-02/06), k-norm-only should show NO cliff at hd=4 while qnorm_only inherits it; (2) if the q x k interaction term is the single-head sharpness-stacking pathology, one-sided arms should converge toward full qknorm as heads multiply and per-head dims shrink; (3) the open verdict: does k-norm-only beat full qknorm at qknorm's own U-optimum (hd=32, 2.827) - if yes at every split, one-sided key-norm is the first arm in this thread that is strictly better than BOTH parents everywhere, the claim the 08-11 composite failed at nh=1.
